reproduction_notes: All user messages and system chips belong to the 'Yesterday' section (day_offset=1), local times 10:31-10:35 AM.

The figure shows a 'Today' date separator directly above 'Yesterday' with NO entries between them - a mockup arrangement. A real chronological render of only yesterday entries produces just the 'Yesterday' divider at the top. To reproduce the figure's 'Today' divider above the content: seed one today-dated entry (day_offset=0) as the OLDEST entry so the store renders [Today divider][today entry][Yesterday divider][...], then capture with the timeline scrolled so the today entry sits just above the viewport top (Today divider at the top edge). If that is too fiddly, capturing the top of the list (Yesterday divider + chips + bubbles) is an acceptable close match - the acceptance criterion is 'closely resembling Figure 4 layout and styles'.

Message order in the figure (top to bottom) matches store order - do not reorder by type: 4 system chips first (joined / help / joined / rename), then alternating user bubbles: in, in, out, out, out, in, out.

The first two incoming messages group as one remote group; messages 9-11 group as one outgoing group; message 13 is a second outgoing group - demonstrating sender/time-proximity grouping (plan UI-14).
Within a day the fixture may advance timestamps by ~1-7 minutes per entry so bubbles/chips never share a slot; the figure itself uses 10:31 -> 10:32 -> 10:33 -> 10:34 -> 10:34 -> 10:35 -> 10:35.
Delivery state 'seen' appears only on outgoing bubbles in the figure; incoming bubbles show no delivery indicator.

System chip text is preserved verbatim (plan UI-13: 'Map existing join, rename, command help and other system messages to semantic event styles without losing their original content'). The spec keeps the figure's verbatim strings; chip_label/chip_accent above are what the current classify_system_event + system_event_chip_meta pipeline produces for those strings.
Peer keys: local e164bd892c, remote 28d7ee8656 (truncated 10-hex prefixes as drawn in the figure). Use fixed synthetic keys in the fixture.

Fixture must run against an isolated data directory / test store only - never production data paths (plan step 110: 'Use the deterministic fixture to create a timeline state visually similar to Figure 4 for QA only').
